title: Ode to Joy
description: Beethoven's big tune from the 9th Symphony. It hardly ever moves more than one key at a time, so it makes a great first melody.

steps.title: A tune from Beethoven's 9th
steps.description: Beethoven wrote this for the last movement of his Ninth Symphony, finished in 1824, setting a poem by Friedrich Schiller. Today it's also the anthem of the European Union. The melody uses just five notes, C D E F G, and mostly moves one key at a time, so your hand can stay put. Rest your thumb on middle C and put one finger on each white key up to G.

steps.title: Phrase 1: E E F G
steps.description: Play E twice, then step up to F and G. The tune climbs right from the first note.
steps.hint: E is two white keys up from middle C. With your thumb on C, it's under your middle finger.

steps.title: Phrase 2: G F E D
steps.description: Now walk back down: G F E D. It's the first phrase in reverse, going one step further at the end.
steps.hint: Each note is the next white key down. No skipping.

steps.title: Phrase 3: C C D E
steps.description: Drop down to middle C and play it twice, then climb to D and E. It's the same shape as the opening, just starting lower.
steps.hint: Middle C is under your thumb. Same pattern as phrase 1: one note twice, then two steps up.

steps.title: Phrase 4: E D D
steps.description: Finish the line with E, then D, D. In the song that last D is held for two beats, and stopping on it makes the line sound like it's asking a question.
steps.hint: Step down from E to D, then play D once more.

steps.title: Middle section: D D E C
steps.description: The middle of the tune has more bounce to it. Play D twice, step up to E, then drop to C. These are just its first few notes, but they show you where it's heading.
steps.hint: Start on D, the white key right above middle C. After E, skip down past D to land on C.

steps.title: The C major chord
steps.description: C major sits under the opening of the tune. Play C, E and G together. It's the home chord for this key.
steps.hint: Thumb on C, middle finger on E, little finger on G. Any octave works.

steps.title: The G major chord
steps.description: Remember how the first line ended on D? That D sits over a G chord, which is why the line sounds unfinished, as if it's waiting for an answer. Play G, B and D.
steps.hint: Same shape as C, just starting on G: G, B, D.

steps.title: The whole first line
steps.description: Play the full first line in order: E E F G | G F E D | C C D E | E D D. Aim for an even pulse, like you're walking.
steps.hint: Wrong notes are just ignored, so if you slip, find the right key and carry on. Watch for the drop to C at the start of the third group.

steps.title: Count the notes
steps.description: This whole melody fits under one hand. Which five notes does it use?

steps.title: Where to go next
steps.description: That's the first line of Ode to Joy. The second line starts exactly the same way but ends on C instead of D, so it sounds finished: E E F G | G F E D | C C D E | D C C. Try working it out on your own, then play both lines back to back.
